title: Frequency-Conditioned Privacy Auditing of Fine-Tuned Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.31581v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models are increasingly fine-tuned on sensitive data, where the same person's information may appear multiple times across records. This can cause models to memorize sensitive information, but memorization does not necessarily mean that the information can be recovered. A more serious privacy risk arises when the model begins to reproduce that information during generation. In this paper, we study how often sensitive information must appear in the fine-tuning data before it becomes recoverable. Across four language models, we vary the frequency of email addresses and phone numbers from $1\times$ to $50\times$ and compare standard fine-tuning, gradient clipping, and differentially private training. We find that the number of repetitions required before sensitive information becomes recoverable varies substantially across models. Gradient clipping can delay extraction, but it does not consistently prevent leakage at high rep

translated_title: 微调语言模型的频率条件化隐私审计
translated_abstract: 大语言模型越来越多地在敏感数据上进行微调，其中同一个人的信息可能在多条记录中多次出现。这可能导致模型记住敏感信息，但记忆并不一定意味着该信息可以被恢复。当模型开始在生成过程中重现这些信息时，才会产生更严重的隐私风险。在本文中，我们研究敏感信息在微调数据中必须出现多少次才能变得可恢复。我们在四个语言模型上，将电子邮件地址和电话号码的重复频率从1倍变化到50倍，并比较标准微调、梯度裁剪和差分隐私训练的效果。我们发现，在敏感信息变得可恢复之前所需的重复次数在不同模型之间存在显著差异。梯度裁剪可以延迟信息被提取的时间，但在高重复次数下并不能一致地防止信息泄露。
tldr: 该论文通过将敏感信息（邮箱地址和电话号码）在微调数据中的重复次数从1倍系统地变化到50倍，发现不同语言模型在敏感信息变得可提取前所需的重复阈值差异巨大，且梯度裁剪只能延迟信息泄露而在高重复率下无法可靠地防止泄露。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically varies the repetition frequency of sensitive information (emails and phone numbers) from 1× to 50× across four language models, finding that the repetition threshold before sensitive information becomes extractable varies substantially across models, and that gradient clipping only delays but does not consistently prevent leakage at high repetition rates.
